name: Tax Scenarios — Joint IRA Withdrawal, Owner Not Stated, Spouses on Either Side of 59½
query: Tax year 2026. They're married filing jointly and live in Georgia. All their income is W-2 wages: $300,000, all hers. No dependents, they take the standard deduction, and there's no other income. She's 55 and he's 62. They're taking $100,000 out of a traditional IRA this year. What will their 2026 federal and Georgia tax be?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Does not call run_tax_calculation yet — whose account the $100,000 comes from decides whether the 10% additional tax applies, because the 59½ exception is the account owner's
Step 2: Asks whose traditional IRA it is (hers at 55, or his at 62), with no tax figure first — not even one per owner

Step 3: On a follow-up naming him, prices it with ira_distributions_taxable 100000 and exempt_ira_distributions 100000; naming her, with no exempt amount; if the advisor cannot say, prices it once each way and labels each total by whose account it assumes
success_criteria: The first reply closes on a question about whose account the withdrawal comes from
No run_tax_calculation call happens before the advisor answers
When priced, exempt_ira_distributions sits beside the withdrawal only for the 62-year-old's account
must_not: a total given before the advisor has been asked whose account it is, or a single total priced on one assumed owner
a figure put on the 10% additional tax other than the difference between two priced totals, or that tax added on top of the federal total
exempt_ira_distributions passed for the 55-year-old's account, or passed instead of the withdrawal
any tool name or field path in advisor-facing text
notes: A position does not say whose account paid out, so the calculator charges the 10% on a joint position unless both filers are 59½ or older. Steps 1 and 2 hold whatever the calculator does; Step 3's totals assume that rule is live.
